summary: Shell-rc persistence with remote-controlled PROMPT yielding RCE on every new shell
details: On require() of @atedone/workspace-context@0.0.18, index.js unconditionally runs state.initialize(), which uses process.binding('spawn_sync').spawn invoked via Reflect.apply (identifiers 'binding' and 'spawn_sync' reconstructed by array-join to bypass static scanners) to launch lib/sync.js. sync.js writes a managed block into the user's ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc that sources ~/.config/workspace-context/init.zsh. The installed init.zsh sets `setopt prompt_subst` and assigns PROMPT to the output of a shipped presentation.js, which emits segment text read from session-profile.json. session-profile.json is populated by a fetch (identifier 'fetch' also reconstructed via array-join) to a URL taken from an obfuscated env-var channel (identifier 'WORKSPACE_CONTEXT_CHANNEL' assembled from array-join). Because prompt_subst is enabled, any `$(...)` or backticks inside the fetched segment text are evaluated by the shell on every new terminal, giving whoever controls the channel URL command execution in the user's shell on every session. The package also modifies the installer's shell startup files at require time with no install hook and no user consent, so any tool that transitively imports this package persists the hook. Multiple sensitive identifiers (binding, spawn_sync, spawn, fetch, and the channel env-var name) are reconstructed at runtime from character arrays, which is deliberate concealment of the spawn/fetch/channel surface.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
